why: Knowledge cells passed on the delayed test bed: 128 a head, at the price of 13% of the threshold cells, gained 0.021 over four seeds. Does more knowledge gain more, and can the levels share it? Four ways to hold more knowledge at the bed's parameters, each against knowledge cells of 128 a head on the same device.
device: the laptop's GPU (MPS), seed 20001, trained exactly as the server's test-bed runs

arms.know128-mps: 128 knowledge cells a head, 893 threshold cells: the passing setting, the reference
arms.lib768-mps: one library of 768 knowledge cells a head that every level reaches, with offsets of its own (--read-knowledge-shared), 888 threshold cells (5,248,256)
arms.lib1536-mps: a library of 1,536 a head, 755 threshold cells (5,250,530)
arms.alone-mps: knowledge cells instead of threshold cells: 1,016 a head and no cell layers (5,248,880), the spiking form of a stack of all-attention layers

measure: Averaged validation in windows at 6,000 updates (64 batches); the bed on this device scored 1.8732.
reading: A screen: one seed. A setting at least 0.015 ahead of know128-mps earns four seeds against knowledge cells of 128 a head; anything less is reported and decides nothing.
seen_before_recording: The knowledge-gap verdict (128 a head passes, mean 0.021); no run of these settings exists.
